issues.legal_issue: A prior mortgagee who purchases the mortgaged property in execution and thereby acquires the equity of redemption has priority over a later-mortgage purchaser in the competing rights to redeem.
material_facts: The owner created an earlier mortgage and later mortgages over the same property.
The earlier mortgagee sued without joining the later mortgagees, and there was no finding that their omission was designed to prejudice them.
The earlier mortgagee purchased the property in execution of the earlier mortgage decree and later transferred his interest.
A later mortgagee subsequently obtained an execution-sale purchase subject to the earlier mortgage, and the competing purchasers asserted rights to redeem.
issues.conclusion: The purchaser under the earlier mortgage acquired the equity of redemption and had the preferential right to redeem the later mortgages over the purchaser under the later mortgages.
issues.legal_principle: The court applied the mortgage principle that a later mortgagee may redeem an earlier mortgage, but an earlier mortgagee who purchases the property in execution acquires the mortgagor’s equity of redemption and has the superior, last right of redemption against later mortgagees. No statutory provision or earlier case was cited.

rule.if: competing_mortgage_redemption_case and prior_mortgagee_execution_purchase and prior_buyer_acquired_redemption_equity and junior_purchase_subject_to_prior_mortgage

predicates.competing_mortgage_redemption_case: The dispute concerns competing purchasers under execution sales on successive mortgages who each claim a right to redeem.
predicates.prior_mortgagee_execution_purchase: The holder of the earlier mortgage purchased the mortgaged property in execution of that mortgage decree.
predicates.prior_buyer_acquired_redemption_equity: The earlier-mortgage purchaser acquired the mortgagor’s equity of redemption through the execution purchase.
predicates.junior_purchase_subject_to_prior_mortgag: A purchaser under a later mortgage obtained the property subject to the earlier mortgage.

issues.definition: When competing purchasers in a mortgage-redemption dispute include an execution purchaser under the earlier mortgage who acquired the equity of redemption and a later-mortgage purchaser whose purchase remained subject to the earlier mortgage, the earlier-mortgage purchaser has the preferential right to redeem.

issues.legal_issue: A court may determine competing redemption priorities in the proceeding before it rather than require a separate suit when the preferential claim has been raised and the opposing claimant had notice of it.
material_facts: The preferential redemption claim was pleaded as an alternative in related litigation rather than in a suit instituted by the competing purchaser.
The competing purchaser had notice of that claim in the proceedings.
The High Court determined the priority between the rival redemption claims instead of requiring another suit.
issues.conclusion: On these facts, the High Court’s decision to determine the priority between the rival redemption claims in the existing litigation was not illegal or improper.
issues.legal_principle: The court accepted the case-specific exercise of deciding the competing redemption priority in the existing litigation where the alternative claim had been raised and the opposing claimant had notice. No statutory provision or earlier case was cited.

predicates.competing_redemption_priority_proceeding: A court is considering rival claims to priority between purchasers asserting rights of redemption.
predicates.preferential_claim_raised_in_related_lit: A claimant raised the preferential redemption claim as an alternative in related litigation rather than instituting the proceeding then under consideration.
predicates.opposing_claimant_had_notice: The opposing claimant had notice of the preferential claim during the litigation.

issues.definition: When rival redemption priorities are before a court, the preferential claim was raised in related litigation, and the opposing claimant had notice, deciding the priority in the existing litigation is not improper.

issues.legal_issue: A transferee of the interest acquired by a prior mortgagee at an execution sale is entitled to possession when that prior mortgagee has the preferential right to redeem the later mortgages.
material_facts: The earlier mortgagee purchased the property in execution and later transferred his interest.
The transferees claimed possession of the property against persons occupying it under the earlier mortgagee.
The court upheld the earlier mortgagee’s preferential right to redeem the later mortgages.
issues.conclusion: The transferees of the earlier mortgagee’s interest were entitled to possession of the property.
issues.legal_principle: The court held that, once the earlier mortgagee’s preferential redemption right was established, the transferees of that mortgagee’s interest were entitled to possession. No statutory provision or earlier case was cited.

predicates.possession_claim_by_prior_mortgagee_tran: A transferee of an earlier mortgagee’s interest claims possession of the mortgaged property.
predicates.prior_mortgagee_preferential_redemption_: The earlier mortgagee has been found to have the preferential right to redeem the later mortgages.
predicates.prior_mortgagee_interest_transferred: The earlier mortgagee transferred the interest acquired through the execution purchase to another person.

issues.definition: When a transferee of an earlier mortgagee’s interest claims possession, the earlier mortgagee has the preferential redemption right, and that interest was transferred, the transferee is entitled to possession.
